routes.description: Establish that the relevant conception of God remains coherent when maximal attributes are defined through genuine logical possibilities, divine knowledge is reconciled with freedom, and apparent bodily, temporal, or infinite-task limitations are distinguished from genuine deficits of power.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it supplies a mutually consistent account of maximal power, knowledge, goodness, embodiment, and temporality that answers the quantitative-infinity objection and preserves a recognizable burden-relevant conception of theism.

motionBridge.description: Show that the divine attributes relevant to the motion admit a jointly coherent interpretation without requiring impossible quantitative magnitudes.

centralBridges.description: Define maximal power by the range of logically possible actions and explain why unrestricted ability need not be an impossible quantitative infinity.
Specify the extent of divine knowledge consistently with divine freedom and explain how any restriction relates to the relevant theistic conception.
Show that apparent limitations arising from embodiment, temporality, or supertasks concern incoherent descriptions or category distinctions rather than absent genuine powers.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Connect the defended attribute set to historically or explanatorily relevant theism rather than assuming that every maximal quantitative formulation is mandatory.
Explain how evaluative knowledge and freedom from conflicting desires can make perfect goodness compatible with the defended account of omnipotence.

routes.description: Establish that the stipulated maximal conception of God requires impossible infinite quantities of power, knowledge, or intelligence, and show that proposed restrictions or reinterpretations either fail to remove those infinities or generate further conflicts among divine attributes and doctrines.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if maximal theism cannot avoid impossible non-extensive infinities without relinquishing motion-relevant attributes, or if its proposed repairs produce contradictions involving freedom, timelessness, embodiment, action, or completed infinite processes.

motionBridge.description: Show that the motion-relevant maximal divine attributes require impossible magnitudes or otherwise cannot be jointly instantiated coherently.

centralBridges.description: Establish that all-powerfulness and comprehensive cognition require unbounded or infinite quantities rather than merely a finite list of action kinds or truths.
Show that limiting foreknowledge or redescribing actions does not eliminate the infinite power, information, or intelligence implicated by the remaining attributes.
Demonstrate that proposed repairs involving timelessness, bodilessness, or temporal-event analysis conflict with other theistic commitments or fail on their own terms.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish allegedly possible extensive infinities from the impossible quantitative infinities attributed to divine power and cognition.
Test abstract coherence defenses against incarnation, changing divine intentions, and completed infinite-action cases that expose their material implications.

sections.title: Maximal power and quantitative infinity
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on whether omnipotence can be understood as a coherent range of abilities or necessarily entails an impossible infinite magnitude of power.

sections.title: Divine knowledge, freedom, and the relevant theistic conception
sections.rationale: The scope of divine knowledge determines whether omniscience conflicts with freedom and whether restricting foreknowledge preserves the conception of theism placed in issue.

sections.title: Actual infinity, divisibility, and supertasks
sections.rationale: Spatial division and the lamp supertask test the parties' competing accounts of actual infinity, temporally extended action, and the implications of unrestricted divine agency.

sections.title: Bodilessness, incarnation, and divine action
sections.rationale: The relationship between necessary bodilessness and incarnation determines whether bodily inabilities are merely logical exclusions or internal tensions within the relevant theology.

sections.title: Timelessness, change, and foreknowledge
sections.rationale: Timelessness offers a possible reconciliation of knowledge and control of the future, while divine changes of intention test whether that reconciliation is internally consistent.
